paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: you can do everything right and still suffer, and Peter says you are blessed anyway. He says, "Do not fear what they fear; do not be shaken." (1 Peter 3:14) That's not a promise that life gets easy. It's a promise that fear doesn't get to run your kitchen.

So what do you do instead? Peter says, "in your hearts sanctify Christ as Lord." (1 Peter 3:15) When Christ is the one you honor most in your heart, people have a hard time scaring you into silence. And when somebody asks about your hope, you answer with "gentleness and respect," with a clear conscience, so that those who slander you "may be put to shame by your good behavior in Christ." (1 Peter 3:15-16)

Why can a baker stand like that? Because Christ "suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God." (1 Peter 3:18) He was put to death, and He was made alive. He is now at the right hand of God, with angels, authorities and powers subject to Him. (1 Peter 3:22) So when the hard day comes, friend, you're not facing it alone and you're not facing it with a loser. You belong to the One who has the last word.
